PullRequest.Title: Chat: distinguish question carousel link states
PullRequest.Body:
Chat question carousel links now react visibly to hover and press across Light 2026, Dark 2026, and high-contrast themes without changing link styling elsewhere.

### Changes

- Add a carousel-scoped underline and stronger interaction stroke for hover and active links, including a perceptible high-contrast state while preserving the existing resting underlines.
- Use the theme focus border for keyboard-only link focus.
- Add real-widget Playwright coverage for rest, hover, active, and keyboard-focus states in light, dark, and both high-contrast fixture variants.

### Validation

- 82 targeted question carousel unit tests passed.
- 4 real-widget Playwright interaction tests passed; all 4 fail against the untouched `origin/main` baseline.
- Component fixture test TypeScript check passed.
- ESLint passed for the new Playwright test.
- Stylelint passed for the carousel stylesheet with 4 pre-existing design-token suggestions.
- Component Explorer compiled successfully and commit-bound before/after captures were verified at identical dimensions, viewport, scale, zoom, fixture, and interaction state.

Fixes #334651

Scenarios.Scenario: A user hovers, presses, or keyboard-focuses a Markdown link in the visible chat question carousel.
Scenarios.CriticalPath: The browser matches the scoped pseudo-class selector and updates link decoration/outline during the interaction. No script, layout measurement, serialization, filesystem, IPC, subprocess, database, or network operation must complete; the change is limited to style recalculation and paint. Outline does not participate in layout, and text-decoration thickness does not alter carousel geometry.
Scenarios.ScalingInput: Effective cardinality is the anchors in the currently rendered carousel, with only the hovered/active/focus-visible anchor acquiring the new declarations. The carousel renders one current question at a time and the dynamic pseudo-class targets one interaction target, so cost does not fan out across question history.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: One renderer-main-thread style/paint update per current pointer or focus transition; interactions are serialized by the browser event loop and the changed CSS does not create workers, queues, listeners, or asynchronous work.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: The stylesheet is loaded through the existing carousel CSS import. Cold and warm behavior are unchanged apart from normal selector matching; there is no new cache, cache key, invalidation path, or cache miss boundary.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High confidence from the changed CSS declarations and traced carousel DOM construction: the diff adds only underline/outline paint properties and no runtime JavaScript or boundary call.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: Exact style-recalculation and paint duration varies by browser and link glyph count, but the changed declarations are bounded, do not trigger layout, and apply only during explicit interaction.
Scenarios.Verdict: No reportable regression. The intentional interaction-state repaint is bounded to the active link and introduces neither synchronous layout work nor collection-scaled rendering.

Scenarios.Scenario: Component-fixture CI runs the new carousel-link interaction coverage across four themes.
Scenarios.CriticalPath: Each of four generated tests waits for one localhost fixture page load, then performs bounded hover, active, keyboard-focus, computed-style, and assertion steps. These operations are on the test job's critical path, but they do not affect product startup or interaction latency.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Navigate one browser page to the local component-explorer fixture and wait for load/visibility.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: Exactly four added localhost navigations, one for each fixed theme variant; no tested link is clicked and therefore no external URL is requested.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: This spec did not exist, so these four fixture navigations were absent; the shared component-explorer server and Playwright suite infrastructure already existed.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Each local page load must complete before its corresponding test can inspect styles.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Drive Chromium through Playwright for hover, mouse, keyboard, DOM evaluation, and computed-style inspection.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: Four fixed test cases. Each has a bounded command sequence; keyboard focus is capped at 20 Tab attempts, yielding constant worst-case automation calls rather than input-scaled fan-out.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: No automation commands for these four carousel-link state cases existed before this diff; the underlying Playwright browser process and protocol were already part of the fixture-test job.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Automation commands and browser responses are serialized within each test and must finish before assertions complete.

Scenarios.ScalingInput: Fixed at four theme entries and one first-link target per fixture. The 20-attempt keyboard loop is a hard cap, not proportional to repository, workspace, history, or user data size.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: The four tests are independent and scheduled by the existing Playwright worker policy; within each test, awaited browser commands are serialized. The diff adds no explicit Promise.all, unbounded parallelism, subprocess launch, or separate web server.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: All cases use the existing shared component-explorer server. Browser page/resource caching may reduce later fixture loads, but the regression assessment does not depend on cache hits because the added test count is fixed and small; there is no new persistent or unbounded cache.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High confidence from the generated four-test loop, openFixture's single page.goto, the capped focus loop, and the existing Playwright/webServer configuration.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: Runner speed and Playwright worker count vary in CI, but total added boundary cardinality is statically bounded at four page loads and a small fixed command sequence.
Scenarios.Verdict: No reportable performance regression. The test-only CI time increase is deliberate, constant, and bounded, with no product impact or concurrency burst.

Analysis.Summary: Completed the performance pass over the full two-file diff. Checked rendering/layout behavior, interaction frequency, selector scope, lifecycle, test automation boundaries, cache behavior, and effective concurrency. No high-confidence actionable performance regression or regression fix was identified.
